prompts.greet_morning: Good morning. My name is Helen, and I'm your examiner today. Can you tell me your full name, please?
prompts.greet_afternoon: Good afternoon. My name is Helen, and I'm your examiner today. Can you tell me your full name, please?
prompts.greet_evening: Good evening. My name is Helen, and I'm your examiner today. Can you tell me your full name, please?
prompts.call: Thank you. And what shall I call you?
prompts.from: And can you tell me where you're from?
prompts.p1_work_1: Thank you. Now, in this first part of the test, I'd like to ask you some questions about yourself. Let's talk about what you do. Do you work, or are you a student?
prompts.p1_work_2: What do you enjoy most about it?
prompts.p1_work_3: Is there anything you find difficult about it?
prompts.p1_morn_1: Now let's talk about mornings. Are you a morning person?
prompts.p1_morn_2: What do you usually do in the first hour after you wake up?
prompts.p1_morn_3: Has your morning routine changed since you were a child?
prompts.p1_morn_4: Is there anything you would like to change about your mornings?
prompts.p1_gift_1: Let's move on to talk about gifts. Do you enjoy choosing presents for other people?
prompts.p1_gift_2: What was the last present you received?
prompts.p1_gift_3: Do you think it's better to give money or a present? Why?
prompts.p2_intro: Thank you. Now, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. I'd like you to describe a skill that took you a long time to learn.
prompts.p2_start: All right? Remember, you have one to two minutes for this, so don't worry if I stop you. I'll tell you when the time is up. Can you start speaking now, please?
prompts.p2_more: Is there anything else you can tell me about it?
prompts.p2_round_1: Do you still use this skill today?
prompts.p2_round_2: Would you like to learn another skill like this one in the future?
prompts.p3_1: Thank you. We've been talking about a skill you learned, and I'd like to discuss with you one or two more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all learning practical skills. What practical skills do you think young people should learn at school?
prompts.p3_2: Is it better to learn a skill from a teacher or from online videos? Why?
prompts.p3_3: Why do you think some people give up when they are learning something new?
prompts.p3_4: Let's move on to talk about skills and work. Which skills do you think will be most valuable for workers in the future?
prompts.p3_5: Some people say that technology is making many traditional skills disappear. Do you think this is a problem?
prompts.p3_6: Should employers pay for their staff to learn new skills, even when those skills are not directly related to their job?
prompts.end: Thank you. That is the end of the speaking test.
